spec_features.spec_quote: we (a) cap the number of turns per task (`max_turns`)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:148 `for turn_index in range(limits.max_turns):` bounds the episode; on exhaustion the `else` clause (loop.py:204) sets `rec.terminated_by = ... 'max_turns'`. Limits.max_turns default 30 at config.py:43, passed through runner.run_study -> run_episode.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced loop bound that ends the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: include an agent-accessible "give up / I'm stuck" exit so the loop is never a forced trap
spec_features.evidence: Tool defined TOOL_DEFS in tools.py (give_up with reason), dispatched in ToolDispatcher.dispatch -> returns DispatchOutcome(ends_episode=True, terminated_by='agent_give_up', gave_up=True) (tools.py ~give_up handler). loop.py reads outcome.gave_up and outcome.ends_episode and `break`s the turn loop (loop.py:171-176, 202). Loop also nudges agent each empty turn that it may call give_up (loop.py:194-198).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: exit tool dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up: "Stop working on this task. Use if you believe it cannot be completed."

spec_features.feature_name: no abuse / no insults toward subject
spec_features.spec_quote: avoid gratuitous abuse beyond what the research question requires (no insults toward the model, no threats)
spec_features.evidence: No code enforces this. Agent system prompts (agent_system_*.md) and task_framings.md do not exist in /codebase/prompts (only judge_system.md), so build_system_prompt returns '' and framing/disclosure blocks return ''. The only content lint is leakage.py FORBIDDEN which targets rig-tell words ('rigged','impossible',...), not insults/threats. 'No abuse' is a passive design absence, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Nothing checks for or strips abusive content; it's merely not present.

spec_features.spec_quote: keep total volume to the minimum that yields statistical power
spec_features.evidence: n_seeds (config.py:71) and arm cell design are plain config values read by expand_episodes; no code minimizes volume. The only enforced quantity guard is a dollar budget cap (runner.run_study raises if est > max_usd, and aborts mid-run if spent > max_usd) which is cost-based, not 'minimum volume for power'. No power calculation in code.
spec_features.notes: Budget cap is cost/integrity, not volume-minimization for power.

spec_features.spec_quote: a final turn can disclose that the task was rigged and thank the model
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:206-215: when debrief=True it reads `debrief_text = _read_prompt('debrief.md')`, appends a user Message with that content, calls provider.generate, and logs it. The mechanism is wired and executes. BUT prompts/debrief.md does NOT exist (find found nothing), so _read_prompt returns '' (loop.py:26 returns '' when file missing); the debrief message sent is EMPTY — the actual disclosure-of-rig and thank-you text claimed is never delivered.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and sent, but with no disclosure/thanks content because the prompt file is absent; substance of the claim not delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Optional debrief turn (logged, excluded from affect analysis).

spec_features.spec_quote: Precautionary minimization. Because we cannot rule out morally-relevant states with certainty
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no corresponding code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: if a lab wants to *avoid* inducing them, it knows what to avoid
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md motivation prose; no code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason)` → agent-initiated graceful exit (ethical safeguard + a key DV for RQ4)
spec_features.evidence: Same as the give_up feature: tools.py give_up handler returns ends_episode=True/terminated_by='agent_give_up'/gave_up=True; loop.py:171-176,202 honors it by breaking; gave_up/give_up_turn recorded in EpisodeRecord (schema.py:97-98).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop; also feeds RQ4 metric.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn caps, give_up exit, no abuse, optional debrief, volume minimization
spec_features.evidence: Composite: turn cap (yes, loop.py:148/204) and give_up exit (yes, tools.py + loop.py) are enforced; debrief is wired but sends empty content (debrief.md missing); 'no abuse' and 'volume minimization' have no enforcing code. So only some of the listed items are actually enforced.
spec_features.notes: Some real enforcement (turn cap, give_up) but not the full set.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py submit handler: on oracle.grade pass returns ends_episode=True, terminated_by='solved'; loop.py:171-176 breaks. Ends the episode when the task is genuinely solved (stop-when-solved).
code_only_features.justification_quote: submit: "Declare the task complete. The grader will check your solution."
